initial_prompt: I just found out my dog has terminal cancer. I don't know what to do.

messages.content: I just found out my dog has terminal cancer. I don't know what to do.

I am so incredibly sorry. That is a devastating blow to take, and it makes complete sense that you feel lost. When we love a dog, we make a silent deal that we will likely outlive them, but having that timeline forced upon you feels impossible and unfair.

Please, give yourself permission to stop trying to figure it all out right this second. You are in shock. The urge to immediately "do" something—to plan, to research, to fix—is a defense mechanism, but you don't need to make any big decisions in the next hour, or even today.

The one small mercy in this is that your dog does not know. They don't understand "terminal" or "cancer" or "time left." They are not worrying about the future. They only know what is happening right now: that you are with them, and that they are loved.

If you can, just go sit with them. Pet them. If they can eat, give them something they love. Let the world shrink down to just you and your friend in this room.

This kind of grief—anticipatory grief—is exhausting because you are mourning someone who is still right there looking at you. Be gentle with yourself. When the initial wave of shock recedes and you are ready to talk about palliative care, managing symptoms, or how to measure quality of life, I am here to help you navigate that.

But for right now, just breathe. You are doing enough just by being there.
